title: Part 2: A Psychohistory of American Psychology: The Myth of Normal and the American Plague

sentences.en: And it was felt in the sleeplessness of every immigrant who had crossed the ocean to find that America was not this golden

sentences.en: The previous generation had known what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 上一代人知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And these were not sophisticated goals, but they were legible.
sentences.zh: 这些目标并不复杂，但它们清晰可见。

sentences.en: And you could measure your progress.
sentences.zh: 你可以衡量自己的进步。

sentences.en: You could tell whether you were succeeding or failing.
sentences.zh: 你可以判断自己是在成功还是失败。

sentences.en: The story had a shape.
sentences.zh: 这个故事是有轮廓的。

sentences.en: All of these previous periods of American history had left us with profound myths.
sentences.zh: 所有这些之前的美国历史时期都给我们留下了深刻的神话。

sentences.en: America had inherited the rugged self-made man mythology from the frontier of
sentences.zh: 美国继承了来自西部边疆的

sentences.en: the WeSt. This was a myth that built the country, the belief that an individual through sheer willpower and physical endurance could carve out a destiny in the wilderness.
sentences.zh: “白手起家的硬汉”神话。这是一个塑造了国家的传说，即个人可以通过纯粹的意志力和身体耐力在荒野中开辟命运。

sentences.en: But in the 1920s, the story had lost its shape.
sentences.zh: 但在 20 世纪 20 年代，这个故事失去了轮廓。

sentences.zh: 边疆已经关闭，铁路已经建成，伟大的工业项目已经

sentences.zh: 完成，美国已成为人类历史上生产力最强的经济体，而没人知道接下来该做什么。

sentences.zh: 这个国家再也不知道该往哪里去了。

sentences.en: But it still inherited that old frontier mythology, and desperately struggled to apply it to a new situation.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然继承了那个古老的边疆神话，并拼命试图将其应用于新的处境。

sentences.en: You can't be a rugged frontiersman in a windowless factory.

sentences.en: Philip Marlowe, but the nation struggled to see itself as a hero, or to find a hero within itself.
sentences.zh: 但这个国家很难将自己视为英雄，或在自身内部找到英雄。

sentences.en: After the myth of the self-made man became so infused with their identity, Americans felt alienated or impoverished by these massive new industrial bureaucracies.
sentences.zh: 在“白手起家”的神话深深融入他们的身份认同后，美国人因这些庞大的新型工业官僚机构而感到疏离或贫困。

sentences.en: They didn't blame the system, but they internalized the failure.

sentences.en: Could it tell

sentences.zh: 心理学可以提供解释，但它提供的解释往往太黑暗、太奇怪、太诚实，或者对人性而言太不讨喜。

sentences.en: Americans wouldn't fully embrace them.
sentences.zh: 美国人不会完全接受它们。

sentences.en: But that's as nothing compared to what happens when our ideas begin to trickle through in whatever garbled form they're relayed to the public.

sentences.zh: 据说他转头对同行者卡尔·荣格（Carl Jung）说，他们还没意识到我们带来的是瘟疫。

sentences.zh: 美国并没有屈服于瘟疫。

sentences.zh: 美国驯化了它。

sentences.en: Freud's 1909 visit was brief.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德 1909 年的访问很短暂。

sentences.en: And over the next three decades, psychology would spread through American culture in ways that Freud never anticipated and would come to deplore.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的三十年里，心理学以弗洛伊德从未预料到且后来会深恶痛绝的方式在美国文化中传播开来。

sentences.zh: 真正的移民潮发生在后来，在更黑暗的环境下。

sentences.zh: 1938 年纳粹吞并奥地利时，弗洛伊德已经 82 岁，且身患癌症。

sentences.en: His books had already been burned in Berlin, and his daughter Anna was becoming a psychologist in her own right.
sentences.zh: 他的书已经在柏林被烧毁，他的女儿安娜（Anna）也已成为一名独立的心理学家。

sentences.en: Through the intervention of powerful friends, Freud escaped to London.
sentences.zh: 在有权势的朋友的干预下，弗洛伊德逃到了伦敦。

sentences.zh: 那是让维多利亚时代的听众感到震惊并成为头条新闻的部分。

sentences.en: Freud's fundamental insight was not that sex was important.
sentences.zh: 更深层、更有趣的主张是，人类并不是自己家园的主人。

sentences.en: That was the part that scandalized Victorian audiences and made for good headlines.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德认为，在意识之下，潜藏着一个广阔的无意识领域，里面充满了我们无法直接触及的欲望、恐惧和记忆。

sentences.zh: 它们塑造着我们的行为、人际关系和选择，如果我们理解了它们，往往会感到恐惧。

sentences.zh: 这太黑暗了。

sentences.en: It could only be partially illuminated.
sentences.zh: 他们想要工具，却不想要背后的哲学。

sentences.en: And for Americans raised on optimism, progress, and the belief that any problem could be solved with sufficient effort, this was too nihilistic.
sentences.zh: 美国将利用这套词汇来构建一种新的心灵英雄神话。

sentences.en: It was too European.
sentences.zh: 受欢迎到底是由什么构成的？

sentences.en: It was too dark.
sentences.zh: 一个人怎样才能在很多人中受欢迎，同时又拥有几个亲密的朋友？

sentences.en: And they wanted the tools without the philosophy.
sentences.zh: 嘿，杰瑞，我们数学课上来了个新女生。

sentences.en: America would use this vocabulary to build a new hero myth of the mind.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，她叫卡罗琳·艾姆斯（Carolyn Ames）。

sentences.en: What is popularity made of anyway?
sentences.zh: 她是个很棒的孩子。

sentences.en: How does a person get to be popular with lots of people and have a few close friends too?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Hey Jerry, there's that new girl in our math class.
sentences.zh: 你认识她吗？

sentences.en: Oh yes, her name's Carolyn Ames.
sentences.zh: 不太熟。

sentences.en: She's a swell kid.
sentences.zh: 我希望我认识她。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 是啊，尤其是当你把它和这个地方的一些怪人相比时。

sentences.en: Do you know her?
sentences.zh: 当精神分析在精英圈层中传播时，一个截然不同的心理学项目正在改变美国社会。

sentences.en: Not very well.
sentences.zh: 那就是统计学意义上的“常态”的创造。

sentences.en: I wish I did.
sentences.zh: 1945 年，克利夫兰医生罗伯特·拉陶·迪金森（Dr. Robert Latao Dickinson）和雕塑家亚伯拉罕·贝尔斯基（Abraham Belsky）揭幕了两座雕像，他们称之为

sentences.en: Yeah, especially when you compare it with some of the weird characters in this place.
sentences.zh: “诺玛”（Norma）和“诺曼”（Norman）。

sentences.en: While psychoanalysis was spreading through elite circles, a very different psychological project was transforming American society.
sentences.zh: 这些人物并非理想化的美女或英雄原型。

sentences.en: The creation of statistical normalcy.
sentences.zh: 它们是由数千名美国人的平均身体测量数据合成而成的。

sentences.en: In 1945, a Cleveland physician named Dr. Robert Latao Dickinson and a sculptor named Abraham Belsky unveiled two statues they called
sentences.zh: 诺玛代表了统计学上的美国女性平均值，而诺曼代表了统计学上的美国男性平均值。

sentences.en: Norma and Norman.
sentences.zh: 这些雕像被誉为科学测量的胜利。

sentences.en: These figures were not idealized beauties or heroic archetypes.
sentences.zh: 终于，这里有了一个客观标准，

sentences.en: They were composites built from the average measurements of thousands of American bodies.
sentences.zh: 美国人可以以此来衡量自己。

sentences.en: Norma represented the statistical average American woman, and Norman represented the statistical average American man.
sentences.zh: 《克利夫兰平原经销商报》甚至赞助了一场比赛，寻找身体比例最接近诺玛的真实女性。

sentences.en: The statues were celebrated as triumphs of scientific measurement.
sentences.zh: 数千名女性提交了她们的测量数据，但最终没有找到获胜者。

sentences.en: Here, finally, was an objective standard to which
sentences.zh: 在这里，终于有了一个客观标准，

sentences.en: Americans could measure themselves.
sentences.zh: 美国人可以以此来衡量自己。

sentences.en: The Cleveland Plain Dealer even sponsored a contest to find the real woman whose body most clearly matched Norma's proportions.
sentences.zh: 《克利夫兰平原经销商报》甚至赞助了一场比赛，寻找身体比例最接近诺玛的真实女性。

sentences.en: Thousands of women submitted their measurements, and no winner was ever found.
sentences.zh: 数千名女性提交了她们的测量数据，但最终没有找到获胜者。

sentences.en: No actual woman matched the statistical average.
sentences.zh: 没有任何真实的女性符合统计学上的平均值。

sentences.en: And this should have been a clue.
sentences.zh: 而这本应是一个线索。

sentences.en: The normal was a mathematical abstraction, not a description of real human beings, definitely not a goal, and not a replacement for America's hero myth.
sentences.zh: “正常”只是一个数学抽象概念，并非对真实人类的描述，更绝非目标，也无法取代美国的英雄神话。

sentences.en: But the concept had already escaped the laboratory.
sentences.zh: 但这个概念早已逃离了实验室。

sentences.en: By the 1920s and 30s, the statistical definition of normalcy had become the goal of American psychology.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪20和30年代，统计学意义上的“正常”定义已成为美国心理学的目标。

sentences.en: The discipline's mandate shifted from treating the sick to defining and enforcing the normal.
sentences.zh: 该学科的使命从治疗病人转变为定义并强制推行“正常”。

sentences.en: This myth of normal became a fiercely weaponized concept.
sentences.zh: 这种“正常”的神话变成了一个被高度武器化的概念。

sentences.en: It was highly weaponized against women who were not allowed to point out exactly what was normal about their own lived experiences,
sentences.zh: 它被极度武器化，用来对付那些不被允许指出自身生活经历中何为“正常”的女性，

sentences.en: and the definition of normalcy was entirely controlled by a medical patriarchy to keep the client compliant, to keep the weirdness away, to stop the other from creeping in.
sentences.zh: 而“正常”的定义完全由医学父权制所掌控，旨在让客户顺从，排斥异类，阻止“他者”的侵入。

sentences.en: A Stepford wives-style psychological containment.
sentences.zh: 这是一种《复制娇妻》式的心理禁锢。

sentences.en: But the myth of normal was equally weaponized to gut men.
sentences.zh: 但“正常”的神话同样被武器化，用来摧毁男性。

sentences.en: Normal, for a man, was defined as being stoic, unemotional, hyperproductive, underthought.
sentences.zh: 对男性而言，“正常”被定义为坚忍、无情、超高产出、不假思索。

sentences.en: And when the
sentences.zh: 而当

sentences.en: Great Depression hit, this manufactured myth of male normalcy structurally crushed men, leaving without a psychological framework to process their own economic castration.
sentences.zh: 大萧条来袭时，这种人为制造的男性“正常”神话从结构上压垮了男性，使他们失去了处理自身经济被“阉割”的心理框架。

sentences.en: This was a subtle but profound transformation.
sentences.zh: 这是一场微妙却深远的转变。

sentences.en: In the old world, there were the sane and the insane, the healthy and the diseased, and the categories were relatively clear.
sentences.zh: 在旧世界里，有正常人和精神病人，有健康人和患病者，这些分类相对清晰。

sentences.en: But the invention of the statistical normal created a vast new territory, the not-quite normal.
sentences.zh: 但统计学上“正常”概念的发明，创造了一个广阔的新领域——“不那么正常”。

sentences.en: And you might not be clinically ill, but you might be anxious in ways that fell outside of the standard deviation.
sentences.zh: 你可能并没有临床意义上的疾病，但你可能会以某种偏离标准差的方式感到焦虑。

sentences.en: Your personality might deviate from your mean.
sentences.zh: 你的个性可能会偏离你的平均值。

sentences.en: Your intelligence or your emotional range, your sexual desires, might fall in the wrong part of the bell curve.
sentences.zh: 你的智力、情感范围或性欲，可能会落在钟形曲线的错误区间。

sentences.en: And the new psychology was less interested in curing dramatic pathologies than in adjusting these subtle deviations.
sentences.zh: 而新的心理学对治愈严重的病理症状兴趣不大，反而更热衷于调整这些细微的偏差。

sentences.en: And it was the goal was to help Americans become more normal, to move towards
sentences.zh: 其目标是帮助美国人变得更“正常”，向

sentences.en: the center of the distribution, to smooth out their eccentricities, to become more like the statistical composite that no actual person resembled.
sentences.zh: 分布的中心靠拢，抹平他们的怪癖，变得更像那个没有任何真实个体与之相符的统计学合成物。

sentences.en: But this just didn't create conformity.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有创造出一致性。

sentences.en: It created hyper-atomization.
sentences.zh: 它创造了极度的原子化。

sentences.en: At the same time that you were striving to be normal, you were also striving to be more normal and better at being normal than everyone around you.
sentences.zh: 当你努力变得“正常”的同时，你也在努力比周围所有人更“正常”、更擅长表现得“正常”。

sentences.en: It put the American psyche into a paradoxical and insane state of competition.
sentences.zh: 这让美国人的心理陷入了一种自相矛盾且疯狂的竞争状态。

sentences.en: It birthed the modern suburb.
sentences.zh: 它催生了现代郊区。

sentences.en: This was a psychology perfectly suited for mass production and mass marketing.
sentences.zh: 这种心理学完美契合了大规模生产和大众营销的需求。

sentences.en: Not only did you need to buy a whole lot of stuff to do everything yourself, like power tools, you also needed to buy a whole lot of stuff
sentences.zh: 你不仅需要购买大量东西来亲力亲为，比如电动工具，你还需要购买大量东西

sentences.en: to make sure that you could do it better than the person next to you, which meant that you had to buy nicer stuff.
sentences.zh: 以确保你能比隔壁的人做得更好，这意味着你必须买更好的东西。

sentences.en: If you could define normal, you could manufacture products for it.
sentences.zh: 如果你能定义“正常”，你就能为它制造产品。

sentences.en: And if you could identify who deviated from normal, then you could sell them solutions.
sentences.zh: 如果你能识别出谁偏离了“正常”，你就能向他们兜售解决方案。

sentences.en: Whether or not you were normal meant that you needed to buy a product.
sentences.zh: 无论你是否“正常”，都意味着你需要购买产品。

sentences.en: The middle of the bell curve became the target market for everything from soap to psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 钟形曲线的中间地带成了从肥皂到心理治疗等一切产品的目标市场。

sentences.en: Mrs. Will Thompson bought a Frigidaire with super freezer.
sentences.zh: 威尔·汤普森夫人买了一台带有超级冷冻室的北极牌冰箱。

sentences.en: The neighbors and friends learned of this new oasis and brought their butter, milk, and eggs for safekeeping.
sentences.zh: 邻居和朋友们得知了这个新绿洲，纷纷把黄油、牛奶和鸡蛋拿来寄存。

sentences.en: The migration to America did not just transform psychoanalysis.
sentences.zh: 向美国的移民潮不仅改变了精神分析学。

sentences.en: It also determined which versions of depth psychology would flourish and which would be marginalized.
sentences.zh: 它还决定了哪些深层心理学流派会蓬勃发展，哪些会被边缘化。

sentences.en: Freud was not the only game in town.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德并非唯一的选择。

sentences.en: By the 1920s, two of his most brilliant former disciples had broken with him and developed their own approaches, Alfred Adler and Carl Jung.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪20年代，他最出色的两名前门徒阿尔弗雷德·阿德勒和卡尔·荣格已与他分道扬镳，并发展出了各自的理论体系。

sentences.en: Both offered visions of the human mind that were in many ways more compatible with American sensibilities than Freud's pessimistic theory.
sentences.zh: 两人提出的心灵观在许多方面比弗洛伊德悲观的理论更符合美国人的感性认知。

sentences.en: But neither would achieve the heights that psychoanalysis would reach.
sentences.zh: 但两者都未能达到精神分析学所企及的高度。

sentences.en: Alfred Adler was the first major defector from Freud's inner circle.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德·阿德勒是弗洛伊德核心圈中第一位主要的背离者。

sentences.en: He had developed what he called individual psychology.
sentences.zh: 他发展出了所谓的“个体心理学”。

sentences.en: Where Freud emphasized the primacy of sexual drives, Adler focused on the social nature of human beings.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德强调性冲动的首要地位，而阿德勒则关注人类的社会属性。

sentences.en: His central concept was the inferiority complex, the universal human experience of feeling inadequate, and the equal universal striving to compensate.
sentences.zh: 他的核心概念是“自卑情结”，即人类普遍存在的自我感觉不足的体验，以及同样普遍存在的补偿努力。

sentences.en: Adler's psychology was fundamentally optimistic.
sentences.zh: 阿德勒的心理学本质上是乐观的。

sentences.en: He believed that people could change, could grow, and could develop their social feeling and become contributing members of society.
sentences.zh: 他相信人们可以改变、成长，可以发展出社会情感，并成为对社会有贡献的成员。

sentences.en: He was interested in education, in child rearing, in the prevention of mental
sentences.zh: 他关注教育、儿童抚养以及通过建立支持性社区来预防精神

sentences.en: illness, through the creation of supportive community, and he ran guidance clinics in Vienna that were models of democratic accessible mental health care.
sentences.zh: 疾病，他在维也纳开办的指导诊所成为了民主且易于获取的心理健康护理典范。

sentences.en: And this should have appealed to Americans, and in many ways it did.
sentences.zh: 这本应吸引美国人，在许多方面也确实如此。

sentences.en: Adler was enormously popular in the United States during his lifetime.
sentences.zh: 阿德勒在世时在美国极受欢迎。

sentences.en: He lectured widely, and he trained
sentences.zh: 他广泛讲学，培训了

sentences.en: American therapists and influenced a generation of educators and social workers.
sentences.zh: 美国治疗师，并影响了一代教育工作者和社会工作者。

sentences.en: The concept of the inferiority complex entered the common speech.
sentences.zh: “自卑情结”这一概念进入了日常用语。

sentences.en: But Adler never achieved institutional dominance.
sentences.zh: 但阿德勒从未获得体制上的主导地位。

sentences.en: He had no powerful organization to promote his ideas.
sentences.zh: 他没有强大的组织来推广他的思想。

sentences.en: He refused to establish the kind of training institutes that
sentences.zh: 他拒绝建立那种

sentences.en: Freudians would build.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德派所建立的培训机构。

sentences.en: And he was more interested in reaching ordinary people than creating an elite priesthood of analysts.
sentences.zh: 他更热衷于接触普通大众，而不是建立一个精英分析师的祭司阶层。

sentences.en: And so after his death in 37, his ideas dispersed.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在37年去世后，他的思想便四散了。

sentences.en: Carl Jung's fate was different but equally instructive.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·荣格的命运则不同，但也同样具有启发意义。

sentences.en: Jung had been Freud's closest successor, the crown prince of psychoanalysis, until their dramatic break in 1913.
sentences.zh: 荣格曾是弗洛伊德最亲密的继任者，精神分析学的“皇太子”，直到他们在1913年发生剧烈决裂。

sentences.en: Jung could not accept Freud's insistence that sexuality was the primary human drive.
sentences.zh: 荣格无法接受弗洛伊德坚持认为性欲是人类首要驱动力的观点。

sentences.en: He believed that there was something more, something deeper, a spiritual dimension to the psyche that
sentences.zh: 他相信还有更多、更深层的东西，一种弗洛伊德的唯物主义无法容纳的、

sentences.en: Freud's materialism could not accommodate.
sentences.zh: 心灵的精神维度。

sentences.en: A subjectivity akin to William James.
sentences.zh: 一种类似于威廉·詹姆斯所描述的主观性。

sentences.en: To raise our glasses tonight, to wish Dr. Freud, Dr. Jung, and Dr. Adler the very best of luck in their new science.
sentences.zh: 今晚让我们举杯，祝愿弗洛伊德博士、荣格博士和阿德勒博士在他们的新科学领域好运。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 女士们，先生们。

sentences.en: Dr. Freud, may I ask you, what did you find was the most fascinating moment of the conference?
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德博士，请问您觉得这次会议最迷人的时刻是什么？

sentences.en: When they declared my theories had nothing to do with science, but instead were a matter for the police.
sentences.zh: 当他们宣称我的理论与科学毫无关系，反而属于警察管辖范畴的时候。

sentences.en: It's because everything you say is couched in biological terMs. Well, I suppose you would rather I spoke with the spirit.
sentences.zh: 那是因为你所说的一切都包裹在生物学术语中。好吧，我想你更希望我谈论精神。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: But what is spirit?
sentences.zh: 但什么是精神？

sentences.en: Everything.
sentences.zh: 一切。

sentences.en: No, everything that shows what you call spirit has more to do with repressed sexuality.
sentences.zh: 不，所有表现出你所谓“精神”的东西，都与被压抑的性欲有更多关联。

sentences.en: Please gentlemen, not in the middle of the dissent.
sentences.zh: 请各位先生，别在分歧中争论。

sentences.en: Our culture is our spirit, our whole civilization.
sentences.zh: 我们的文化就是我们的精神，是我们整个文明。

sentences.en: Civilization, Carl.
sentences.zh: 文明，卡尔。

sentences.en: And don't tell me it's just a consequence of repressed sexuality.
sentences.zh: 别告诉我这只是被压抑的性欲的结果。

sentences.en: Yes, I'm afraid it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，恐怕正是如此。

sentences.en: The whole dilemma of power, eros, and love seems to be never ending.
sentences.zh: 权力、爱欲和爱的整个困境似乎永无止境。

sentences.en: Well, to quote you, Carl, the pendulum of the mind swings between sense and nonsense, not between right and wrong.
sentences.zh: 好吧，引用你的一句话，卡尔：心灵的钟摆在理智与荒谬之间摆动，而非在对与错之间。

sentences.en: For Jung, the psychological development was not simply about adjusting to society.
sentences.zh: 对荣格而言，心理发展不仅仅是为了适应社会。

sentences.en: It was about individual integration, taking all of the parts of self and then making them understood or conscious so that they could become part of a bigger whole.
sentences.zh: 它是关于个体的整合，将自我的所有部分理解或意识化，从而使它们成为更大整体的一部分。

sentences.en: The process itself was essentially spiritual, and this was too mystical for American medicine.
sentences.zh: 这个过程本质上是精神性的，这对美国医学界来说太神秘了。

sentences.en: Jung's ideas appealed to artists, writers, theologians, and seekers of various kinds.
sentences.zh: 荣格的思想吸引了艺术家、作家、神学家和各种寻求者。

sentences.en: Joseph Campbell, who had spent the 1930s and
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·坎贝尔，他在20世纪30年代和

sentences.en: 1940s developing his theory of the hero's journey, to be published in the 50s, was deeply influenced by
sentences.zh: 40年代发展了他的“英雄之旅”理论，并于50年代出版，他深受

sentences.en: Jung's concept of archetypes.
sentences.zh: 荣格原型概念的影响。

sentences.en: But the medical establishment viewed Jung with suspicion.
sentences.zh: 但医学界对荣格持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: His embrace of religion, his interest in alchemy and mythology, his interest in the psyche, and the spiritual dimension
sentences.zh: 他拥抱宗教，对炼金术和神话感兴趣，对心灵和精神维度的关注，

sentences.en: made him seem unscientific, including his inability to produce any metrics.
sentences.zh: 让他显得不科学，包括他无法提供任何量化指标。

sentences.en: Publishing broad theories and case studies, he stayed away from quantified data.
sentences.zh: 他发表广泛的理论和案例研究，却远离量化数据。

sentences.en: And here we must pause and look at a terrifying parallel.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们必须停下来看看一个可怕的相似之处。

sentences.en: In the previous episode, we saw how American psychology desperately insecure and craving the authority of hard science murdered its own father, William James.
sentences.zh: 在上一集中，我们看到美国心理学是如何因极度不安全感和对硬科学权威的渴望，而杀死了自己的父亲——威廉·詹姆斯。

sentences.en: James embraced the stream of consciousness and the mystical, and he was replaced by John Watson, who offered the sterile mechanicalistic illusion of control.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯拥抱意识流和神秘主义，但他被约翰·华生取代了，后者提供了冷冰冰的、机械化的控制幻觉。

sentences.en: Across the Atlantic, the exact same tragedy played out between Sigmund Freud and
sentences.zh: 在大西洋彼岸，西格蒙德·弗洛伊德和

sentences.en: Carl Jung.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·荣格之间上演了完全相同的悲剧。

sentences.en: And this dynamic was not simply capitalism binding the world.
sentences.zh: 这种动态不仅仅是资本主义在束缚世界。

sentences.en: It was about psychology itself becoming profoundly insecure.
sentences.zh: 这是关于心理学本身变得极度不安全。

sentences.en: Freud was terrified that if psychoanalysis embraced the spiritual or the uncomputable, it would be dismissed by the rigid medical establishment.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德非常害怕，如果精神分析学拥抱精神或不可计算的东西，就会被僵化的医学界所摒弃。

sentences.en: He was largely right.
sentences.zh: 他大体上是对的。

sentences.en: And Freud famously warned Jung that they must take a dogma of sexual theory to act as a bulwark against the black mud of occultism.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德曾有名言警告荣格，他们必须坚持性理论的教条，以作为抵御神秘主义黑泥的堡垒。

sentences.en: Freud and Watson were the institutional enforcers.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德和华生是体制的执行者。

sentences.en: They pushed the mystery of the human soul away to protect their fragile academic authority.
sentences.zh: 他们排斥人类灵魂的奥秘，以保护他们脆弱的学术权威。

sentences.en: And James and Jung were the expansive, messy, mystical explorers who were excommunicated because their ideas couldn't be quantified, controlled, or easily
sentences.zh: 而詹姆斯和荣格是广阔、混乱、神秘的探索者，他们被逐出教会，因为他们的思想无法被量化、控制，也无法被新兴的专家治国体制轻易

sentences.en: monetized by the emerging technocratic state.
sentences.zh: 货币化。

sentences.en: This also has a parallel in what would happen in the 1980s and 90s, when cognitive and behavioral therapy would largely replace psychodynamic and somatic therapy
sentences.zh: 这与20世纪80和90年代发生的事情也有相似之处，当时认知和行为疗法在很大程度上取代了动力学和躯体疗法，

sentences.en: as objective metrics to push away some of the weirdness of the mindfulness-based New Age movement,
sentences.zh: 作为客观指标来排斥基于正念的新时代运动中的某些怪异之处，

sentences.en: when Eastern philosophy would cross-contaminate psychotherapy in California in the early 60s.
sentences.zh: 当时东方哲学在60年代初渗透进了加州的心理治疗领域。

sentences.en: While traditional psychoanalysis debated sexual drives and Oedipus complexes, a German psychoanalyst named
sentences.zh: 当传统的精神分析学还在争论性冲动和俄狄浦斯情结时，一位名叫

sentences.en: Karen Horney arrived in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 卡伦·霍妮的德国精神分析学家

sentences.en: in 1932 and saw something far more urgent.
sentences.zh: 于1932年来到美国，并看到了更紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: Horney realized that in a terrifying environment, human beings are not primarily motivated by primitive drives.
sentences.zh: 霍妮意识到，在令人恐惧的环境中，人类的主要动力并非原始冲动。

sentences.en: They're motivated by the need for security, for love, and what she called basic truSt. Unlike Watson, she didn't think that every variable
sentences.zh: 他们受到对安全感、爱以及她所谓的“基本信任”的需求驱动。与华生不同，她不认为环境的每一个变量

sentences.en: of the environment could control a person.
sentences.zh: 都能控制一个人。

sentences.en: But unlike Freud and Jung, she didn't think that basic inborn drives needed to be discovered in the unconscious.
sentences.zh: 但与弗洛伊德和荣格不同，她不认为需要在潜意识中去发现基本的先天驱动力。

sentences.en: She saw the roots of human attachment to the parent in early childhood as the thing that had the most explaining power about human behavior in adults.
sentences.zh: 她认为童年早期人类对父母的依恋根源，是对成人人类行为最具解释力的因素。

sentences.en: Back to the matter, Muley.
sentences.zh: 回到正题，缪利。

sentences.en: After what them dusters done to the land, the tenant system don't work no more.
sentences.zh: 在那些尘暴干了这些事之后，佃农制度再也行不通了。

sentences.en: They don't even break even, much less show a profit.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至连成本都收不回来，更别提盈利了。

sentences.en: Why, one man in a tractor can handle 12 or 14 of these places.
sentences.zh: 瞧，一个人开着拖拉机就能打理12到14个这样的农场。

sentences.en: You just pay them a wage and take all the crop.
sentences.zh: 你只需要付给他们工资，然后拿走所有的庄稼。

sentences.en: Yeah, but we couldn't do on any less than what our share is now.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但我们现在的分成已经少得不能再少了。

sentences.en: Well, the children ain't get enough to eat as it is.
sentences.zh: 孩子们连饭都吃不饱。

sentences.en: And they're so ragged, we'd be ashamed if everybody else's children wasn't the same way.
sentences.zh: 他们衣衫褴褛，如果不是因为别人的孩子也一样，我们真会感到羞愧。

sentences.en: I can't help that.
sentences.zh: 我对此无能为力。

sentences.en: All I know is I got my orders.
sentences.zh: 我只知道我接到了命令。

sentences.en: They told me to tell you to get off and that's what I'm telling you.
sentences.zh: 他们让我告诉你们搬走，这就是我告诉你们的。

sentences.en: You mean get off my own land?
sentences.zh: 你是说让我搬离自己的土地？

sentences.en: Don't go into blaming me.
sentences.zh: 别怪我。

sentences.en: It ain't my fault.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的错。

sentences.en: Whose fault is it?
sentences.zh: 那是谁的错？

sentences.en: You know who owns the land, the Shawnee Land and Cattle Company.
sentences.zh: 你知道是谁拥有这片土地，肖尼土地与畜牧公司。

sentences.en: And who's the Shawnee Land and Cattle Company?
sentences.zh: 那肖尼土地与畜牧公司又是谁？

sentences.en: It ain't nobody.
sentences.zh: 它什么也不是。

sentences.en: It's a company.
sentences.zh: 它是一家公司。

sentences.en: They got a president, ain't they?
sentences.zh: 他们有总裁，对吧？

sentences.en: They got somebody who knows what a shotgun's for, ain't they?
sentences.zh: 他们总有知道猎枪是干什么用的人吧？

sentences.en: Oh, son, it ain't his fault because the bank tells him what to do.
sentences.zh: 噢，孩子，这也不是他的错，因为银行在指挥他做事。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Where's the bank?
sentences.zh: 银行在哪？

sentences.en: Tulsa.
sentences.zh: 塔尔萨。

sentences.en: What's he used to picking on him?
sentences.zh: 那你干嘛老找他麻烦？

sentences.en: He ain't nothing but the manager.
sentences.zh: 他不过是个经理。

sentences.en: And he's half crazy as self trying to keep up with his orders from the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 他自己也快疯了，正忙着应付来自东部的命令。

sentences.en: Then who do we shoot?
sentences.zh: 那我们该开枪打谁？

sentences.en: Brother, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 兄弟，我不知道。

sentences.en: If I did, I'd tell you.
sentences.zh: 如果我做了，我会告诉你的。

sentences.en: In the middle of the 1930s, America was a fundamentally unsafe place.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代中期，美国是一个从根本上来说不安全的地方。

sentences.en: The frontier was dead, the economy had collapsed, and the nation was suspended in a terrifying void, desperately waiting for a new hero myth to save them.
sentences.zh: 边疆已成往事，经济已经崩溃，整个国家悬浮在一个可怕的虚无之中，绝望地等待着一个新的英雄神话来拯救他们。

sentences.en: In the winter of 1933, President Franklin Roosevelt addressed the American people.
sentences.zh: 1933年冬天，富兰克林·罗斯福总统向美国人民发表了讲话。

sentences.en: His fireside chats were not a traditional speech.
sentences.zh: 他的“炉边谈话”并非传统的演讲。

sentences.en: They were intimate conversations delivered through a medium that had just transformed the country.
sentences.zh: 它们是通过一种刚刚改变了整个国家的媒介所进行的亲密对话。

sentences.en: The media theorist Walter Ong called radio the beginning of a secondary orality.
sentences.zh: 媒体理论家沃尔特·翁将广播称为“次生口语文化”的开端。

sentences.en: It created a voice without a body, intimate without presence, creating the sensation of personal connection across impossible distance.
sentences.zh: 它创造了一种没有实体的声音，在没有现场感的情况下营造出亲密感，在无法逾越的距离之间创造出一种个人连接的错觉。

sentences.en: Radio created a parasocial relationship, the profound feeling of knowing someone that you would never actually met.
sentences.zh: 广播创造了一种准社会关系，即那种深刻地感觉自己认识一个从未谋面之人的心理体验。

sentences.en: And this was a massive nationwide attachment play.
sentences.zh: 而这正是全国范围内一场大规模的依恋游戏。

sentences.en: It was only because of the sheer economic terror of the Great Depression that this medium could be stumbled upon and weaponized in this exact way.
sentences.zh: 正是因为大萧条带来的巨大经济恐慌，这种媒介才得以被偶然发现并以这种精确的方式被武器化。

sentences.en: In a great time of economic surplus, it wouldn't have been needed.
sentences.zh: 如果是在经济盈余的繁荣时期，它根本不需要存在。

sentences.en: But during the Depression, the American male, the traditional paterfamilias, had been economically castrated.
sentences.zh: 但在大萧条期间，美国男性，即传统的“一家之主”，在经济上被“阉割”了。

sentences.en: He no longer felt like the provider.
sentences.zh: 他不再觉得自己是供养者。

sentences.en: Enter FDr.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福登场了。

sentences.en: Throughout the radio, the President effectively threw a warm blanket over a freezing and terrified country.
sentences.zh: 通过广播，总统有效地为这个寒冷而恐惧的国家披上了一条温暖的毯子。

sentences.en: He got cozy with everybody, making the populace feel like they were snuggling in a bed, listening to a wise, protective grandfather.
sentences.zh: 他与每个人拉近距离，让民众感觉就像蜷缩在床上，听着一位睿智、充满保护欲的祖父说话。

sentences.en: And he successfully projected the ultimate Jungian archetype of the father, filling the void left by the death of the American hero.
sentences.zh: 他成功地投射出了荣格心理学中“父亲”的终极原型，填补了美国英雄形象消亡后留下的空白。

sentences.en: But as Jung would understand, this kind of attachment also can have a shadow, the ability for someone to manipulate.
sentences.zh: 但正如荣格所理解的那样，这种依恋也可能存在阴影，即被人操纵的可能性。

sentences.en: Roosevelt wasn't the only one who understood the archetypes that were missing in America or the powerful new media and cultural realities that technology was allowing.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福并不是唯一一个理解美国所缺失的原型，或是理解技术所带来的强大新媒体和文化现实的人。

sentences.en: Edward Bernays was Sigmund Freud's nephew.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·伯内斯是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的侄子。

sentences.en: And where Freud was interested in healing, Bernays wanted power.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德热衷于治愈，而伯内斯追求的是权力。

sentences.en: Bernays' core insight, drawn directly from depth psychology, was that human beings are not rational actors.
sentences.zh: 伯内斯的核心洞见直接源于深度心理学，即人类并非理性的行动者。

sentences.en: To influence mass behavior, you do not appeal to reason.
sentences.zh: 要影响大众行为，你不能诉诸理性。

sentences.en: You appeal to instinct.
sentences.zh: 你要诉诸本能。

sentences.en: And you manufacture desires that people do not know that they have.
sentences.zh: 你要制造出人们自己都不知道自己拥有的欲望。

sentences.en: Bernays staged spectacles.
sentences.zh: 伯内斯策划了各种奇观。

sentences.en: Like having debutantes smoke Lucky Strike cigarettes, a male behavior being done defiantly by women.
sentences.zh: 比如让名媛们抽“好彩”香烟，这是一种男性行为，却被女性挑衅般地效仿。

sentences.en: It looked organic.
sentences.zh: 这看起来很自然。

sentences.en: The women held up signs saying that they were called torches of freedom.
sentences.zh: 女性们举着标语，声称她们手中的香烟是“自由的火炬”。

sentences.en: And Bernays had engineered the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都是伯内斯精心设计的。

sentences.en: He took a genuine political desire, women's equality, and then redirected it towards a consumer behavior, making them both inseparable.
sentences.zh: 他抓住了一种真实的政治诉求——女性平等，然后将其转化为消费行为，使两者变得密不可分。

sentences.en: If you wanted female empowerment, you know how to smoke as a woman.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要女性赋权，你就得知道如何像女性一样抽烟。

sentences.en: The energy of rebellion was captured and commodified.
sentences.zh: 反叛的能量被捕获并商品化了。

sentences.en: And Bernays was explicit in his 1928 book, Propaganda, writing that the intelligent manipulation of the masses is the true ruling power of the country.
sentences.zh: 伯内斯在1928年的著作《宣传》中直言不讳地写道：对大众进行理性的操纵，是这个国家真正的统治力量。

sentences.en: The elite were utilizing an archetypal magic, the mother, the hero, the patriarch, to sell soap, cigarettes, and political compliance, hiding behind the veneer of rational PR.
sentences.zh: 精英们利用着原型魔法——母亲、英雄、族长——来兜售肥皂、香烟和政治顺从，并躲在理性公关的幌子背后。

sentences.en: Crucially, this engineering would soon extend to selling a suburban home as the ultimate psychological sanctuary.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，这种工程学很快就扩展到了将郊区住宅作为终极心理避难所进行兜售。

sentences.en: PR firms and developers utilized these exact same mechanisms to equate citizenship and consumption,
sentences.zh: 公关公司和开发商利用完全相同的机制将公民身份与消费等同起来，

sentences.en: ensuring that the public was primed to retreat into private consumerist fortresses the moment that the coming war ended.
sentences.zh: 确保公众在即将到来的战争结束时，已经做好了退缩进私人消费主义堡垒的准备。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: George, there is a rumor around town that you've closed your doors, is that true?
sentences.zh: 乔治，城里有传言说你关门了，是真的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, well, I'm very glad to hear that.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，听到这个我很高兴。

sentences.en: George, are you all right?
sentences.zh: 乔治，你还好吗？

sentences.en: Do you need any police?
sentences.zh: 你需要警察吗？

sentences.en: Police?
sentences.zh: 警察？

sentences.en: What for?
sentences.zh: 干什么？

sentences.en: Well, mobs get pretty ugly sometimes, you know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，暴民有时候会变得很凶残，你知道的。

sentences.en: George, I am going all out to help in this crisis.
sentences.zh: 乔治，我正在全力帮助应对这场危机。

sentences.en: I have just guaranteed the bank sufficient funds to meet their needs.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚担保银行有足够的资金来满足他们的需求。

sentences.en: They will close up for a week, and then reopen.
sentences.zh: 他们会停业一周，然后重新开业。

sentences.en: Just took over the bank.
sentences.zh: 刚接管了银行。

sentences.en: I may lose a fortune, but I am willing to guarantee your people too.
sentences.zh: 我可能会损失一笔财富，但我愿意为你们的人民提供担保。

sentences.en: Just tell them to bring their shares over here, and I will pay 50 cents on the dollar.
sentences.zh: 只要让他们把股份带到这里来，我会按面值的50美分支付。

sentences.en: Boy, you never miss a trick, do you, Potter?
sentences.zh: 伙计，你从来都不会错过任何机会，对吧，波特？

sentences.en: Or you're gonna miss this one!
sentences.zh: 否则你就会错过这次机会！

sentences.en: If you close your doors before 6pm, you will never reopen.
sentences.zh: 如果你在下午6点前关门，你就永远别想再开业了。

sentences.en: The stock market crash of October 1929 destroyed not just wealth, but the entire American mythology.
sentences.zh: 1929年10月的股市崩盘摧毁的不仅是财富，还有整个美国神话。

sentences.en: Millions lost their jobs and homes.
sentences.zh: 数百万人失去了工作和家园。

sentences.en: And this massive split between the material realities of America and the promises of the American Dream led to a profound reorientation.
sentences.zh: 美国物质现实与“美国梦”承诺之间的巨大裂痕，导致了一场深刻的重新定位。

sentences.en: The American Dream had been presented like a guaranteed contract.
sentences.zh: “美国梦”曾被呈现为一份有保障的合同。

sentences.en: But now the people who had been promised assembly lines were lining up for bread lines.
sentences.zh: 但现在，那些被承诺拥有流水线工作的人，却在排队领救济粮。

sentences.en: And when that happened, the system didn't blame itself.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，体制并没有反思自己。

sentences.en: It started blaming the victim.
sentences.zh: 它开始指责受害者。

sentences.en: Before the Great Depression, poverty in America had a very different psychological texture than poverty in the old world.
sentences.zh: 在大萧条之前，美国的贫困与旧世界的贫困在心理质感上有着本质的不同。

sentences.en: In medieval England or France, poverty was futile.
sentences.zh: 在中世纪的英国或法国，贫困是徒劳的。

sentences.en: It was a permanent structural class that you were born into.
sentences.zh: 那是一个你生来就属于的永久性结构化阶级。

sentences.en: But the American mythos was built on the safety valve of the frontier.
sentences.zh: 但美国的精神内核建立在“边疆安全阀”的基础上。

sentences.en: Poverty was supposed to be a temporary state.
sentences.zh: 贫困本应是一种暂时状态。

sentences.en: If you failed in the east, you could go weSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你在东部失败了，你可以去西部。

sentences.en: Upward mobility wasn't just possible, it was the national religion.
sentences.zh: 向上流动不仅是可能的，更是美国的国教。

sentences.en: By the 1930s, the frontier was closed, and the factories were padlocked.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪30年代，边疆关闭了，工厂也锁上了大门。

sentences.en: Suddenly, America found itself with a permanent, trapped, starving underclass.
sentences.zh: 突然间，美国发现自己出现了一个永久的、被困住的、挨饿的底层阶级。

sentences.en: And for the first time in history, America was staring down the barrel of European-style structural poverty.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上第一次，美国直面了欧洲式的结构性贫困。

sentences.en: The stock market crash broke the illusion.
sentences.zh: 股市崩盘打破了幻觉。

sentences.en: And when the psychological pacification of mass media failed to keep starving people docile, the masks slipped.
sentences.zh: 当大众媒体的心理安抚无法让饥饿的人民保持顺从时，面具就滑落了。

sentences.en: In 1933, wealthy Wall Street elites looked at this new, permanent underclass and became terrified of a European-style communist revolution.
sentences.zh: 1933年，富有的华尔街精英们看着这个新的、永久的底层阶级，开始恐惧欧洲式的共产主义革命。

sentences.en: In a blind panic, they actually attempted to organize a fascist military coup, the infamous Business Plot,
sentences.zh: 在盲目的恐慌中，他们甚至试图组织一场法西斯军事政变，即臭名昭著的“商业阴谋”，

sentences.en: approaching a retired Marine Corps general, General Smedley Butler, to march an army of veterans on Washington to overthrow FDR's government.
sentences.zh: 他们接触了一位退役的海军陆战队少将——斯梅德利·巴特勒将军，企图率领一支退伍军人大军进军华盛顿，推翻罗斯福政府。

sentences.en: The coup was thwarted, but when Butler blew the whistle, the failure of the Business Plot taught the American establishment a terrifying and valuable lesson.
sentences.zh: 政变被挫败了，但当巴特勒揭发此事后，“商业阴谋”的失败给美国建制派上了一堂可怕而宝贵的一课。

sentences.en: In a democracy, you can't control a starving, angry working class with guns and dictatorship.
sentences.zh: 在民主国家，你不能用枪支和独裁来控制饥饿、愤怒的工人阶级。

sentences.en: It's too clumsy.
sentences.zh: 那太笨拙了。

sentences.en: It sparks revolution.
sentences.zh: 它会引发革命。

sentences.en: You have to control their minds.
sentences.zh: 你必须控制他们的思想。

sentences.en: This is why the system doubled down on a new kind of psychological management.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么体制加倍投入了一种新型的心理管理。

sentences.en: If the elites could not use the military to keep the masses in line, then they would find a way to get the masses to keep themselves in line.
sentences.zh: 如果精英们不能利用军队来让大众保持一致，那么他们就会找到一种方法，让大众自己管理自己。

sentences.en: In the feudal system of Europe, class was based around identity.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲的封建制度中，阶级是围绕身份构建的。

sentences.en: But in America, identity was malleable.
sentences.zh: 但在美国，身份是可塑的。

sentences.en: If you failed, then the failure must have been your fault.
sentences.zh: 如果你失败了，那么失败一定是你自己的错。

sentences.en: It was this hyper-internalized shame that would collide with the logistical meat grinder of World War II to make the psychology of the next century.
sentences.zh: 正是这种高度内化的羞耻感，与二战的后勤绞肉机碰撞，塑造了下一个世纪的心理学。

sentences.en: When America entered the war, the military establishment faced an unprecedented demand, sorting millions and millions of men.
sentences.zh: 当美国参战时，军事机构面临着前所未有的需求：筛选数以百万计的士兵。

sentences.en: They did not care about the depths of the human soul, and they didn't care about the debates between Freudians and Jungians.
sentences.zh: 他们不在乎人类灵魂的深度，也不在乎弗洛伊德学派和荣格学派之间的争论。

sentences.en: They just needed metrics.
sentences.zh: 他们只需要指标。

sentences.en: And they needed a standardized baseline of human behavior that could be applied at scale.
sentences.zh: 他们需要一个可以大规模应用的标准化人类行为基准。

sentences.en: So they invented the myth of normal that would later come to define the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 于是他们发明了“正常”的神话，这后来定义了郊区生活。

sentences.en: To process the chaotic reality of combat trauma, the military forced the creation of a standardized logistical sorting manual for psychiatric casualties.
sentences.zh: 为了处理战斗创伤的混乱现实，军方强制创建了一本针对精神伤亡人员的标准化后勤分类手册。

sentences.en: This manual laid the immediate groundwork for what would become the first DSM, or Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.
sentences.zh: 这本手册为后来成为第一版《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）奠定了直接基础。

sentences.en: Crucially, this rigid statistical checklist was pushed through against the wishes of the very psychiatrist who were forced to draft it.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，这份僵化的统计清单是在违背了被迫起草它的精神科医生意愿的情况下强行推行的。

sentences.en: The clinicians knew that human suffering could not be reduced to a spreadsheet, but the spreadsheet had already won.
sentences.zh: 临床医生们知道人类的痛苦无法简化为电子表格，但电子表格已经赢了。

sentences.en: The military's drive to standardize everything bled directly into the civilian world in 1945.
sentences.zh: 军方将一切标准化的动力在1945年直接渗透到了平民世界。

sentences.en: The discipline of psychology shifted its mandate from exploring the depths of the soul to enforcing the baseline of the normal citizen.
sentences.zh: 心理学学科的使命从探索灵魂深处转向了强制执行“正常公民”的基准。

sentences.en: And when you combine these two historical forces, the paralyzing shame of the rugged individual self-made man,
sentences.zh: 当你将这两种历史力量结合起来——“坚韧的个人主义者”那种令人瘫痪的羞耻感，

sentences.en: and the idea of the aggressively normal person, you got the groundwork for the American suburb.
sentences.zh: 以及“极度正常的人”这一概念，你就得到了美国郊区的基石。

sentences.en: The ultimate absurdity is that absolutely no one working in these psychological systems at this time thought of psychiatry like a system that was objective or quantifiable.
sentences.zh: 最荒谬的是，当时在这些心理学系统中工作的任何人，都没有把精神病学看作是一个客观或可量化的系统。

sentences.en: Freud, Jung, Adler, none of them.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德、荣格、阿德勒，他们都没有。

sentences.en: Only John B.
sentences.zh: 只有约翰·B·

sentences.en: Watson and the behaviorists actually believed that you could measure the human mind like a machine.
sentences.zh: 华生和行为主义者才真正相信你可以像测量机器一样测量人类的心智。

sentences.en: The military establishment grabbed the wriggling, aqueous body of the discombobulated scene that was American psychology,
sentences.zh: 军事机构抓住了美国心理学那混乱、流动的躯体，

sentences.en: and they forced it into the rigid reductivism of the Taylorists, the Watsonian behaviorists, and the systems thinkers.
sentences.zh: 强行将其塞进了泰勒主义者、华生行为主义者和系统思想家那僵化的还原论框架中。

sentences.en: Like James had envisioned it, psychotherapy was still a pretty subjective process.
sentences.zh: 正如詹姆斯所设想的那样，心理治疗仍然是一个相当主观的过程。

sentences.en: It was about the relationship between nodes, the relationships between people, and that blank space was the medicine.
sentences.zh: 它关乎节点之间的关系，关乎人与人之间的关系，而那片空白空间就是良药。

sentences.en: The change made at this time would turn the system into symptoms and interventions for the rest of its existence.
sentences.zh: 当时所做的改变将使该系统在余下的存在时间里，只剩下症状和干预措施。

sentences.en: It's something that nobody planned and that nobody at the time thought was possible, but it happened all without anyone noticing.
sentences.zh: 这是没人计划过、当时也没人认为可能发生的事情，但它在无人察觉的情况下发生了。

sentences.en: And if you asked Adler, Freud, or Jung about this, what would they say?
sentences.zh: 如果你问阿德勒、弗洛伊德或荣格关于这件事的看法，他们会怎么说？

sentences.en: Freudian psychoanalysis was essentially Freud wanting to study people.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德的精神分析本质上是弗洛伊德想要研究人类。

sentences.en: He thought that there were dark and unreconcilable forces and your best bet was just to take a little peek at them,
sentences.zh: 他认为存在着黑暗且无法调和的力量，你最好的办法就是窥探它们一眼，

sentences.en: think about how powerless you are, appreciate the gravity of that interpretation, and then move on.
sentences.zh: 思考一下你是多么无力，领会这种解读的严重性，然后继续前行。

sentences.en: He would be appalled to see his priest class of interpreters replaced by a checkliSt.
sentences.zh: 看到他那作为“祭司阶层”的解读者被一份清单所取代，他会感到震惊。

sentences.en: Carl Jung thought that people had distinct parts of self that play different roles in society and came from different parts of history and different evolutionary needs of a system.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·荣格认为，人们拥有自我的不同部分，这些部分在社会中扮演不同的角色，源于历史的不同部分以及系统不同的进化需求。

sentences.en: And he believed that you should prepare for death as the ultimate state of life, looking for the structure of narrative and the structure of anthropological society
sentences.zh: 他相信你应该为死亡这一生命的终极状态做好准备，寻找叙事结构和人类社会结构，

sentences.en: to model how a person finds meaning while they move through life and age.
sentences.zh: 以模拟一个人在经历生命和衰老的过程中如何寻找意义。

sentences.en: You cannot stream for that like a disease.
sentences.zh: 你不能像对待疾病一样去筛查这种东西。

sentences.en: And Alfred Adler thought that our neuroses were internal compensatory mechanisms for social dysfunction that showed up externally and could be mapped in social interaction.
sentences.zh: 而阿尔弗雷德·阿德勒认为，我们的神经症是社会功能障碍的内部补偿机制，它们在外部表现出来，并可以在社会互动中被映射出来。

sentences.en: None of this is compatible with the system it's been forced into, but it still uses their language.
sentences.zh: 这一切都与它被强行塞入的系统不兼容，但它仍然在使用他们的语言。

sentences.en: The terms are still around in the DSM.
sentences.zh: 这些术语在DSM中依然存在。

sentences.en: And there are concepts that are completely irreconcilable with the diagnostic checklist
sentences.zh: 而且有些概念与诊断清单完全无法调和，

sentences.en: because there are forces that move across time and in-between things, not things that can be screened for.
sentences.zh: 因为有些力量是在时间中和事物之间流动的，而不是可以被筛查出来的东西。

sentences.en: And so this bizarre fusion, this deep subjective theory of these three thinkers,
sentences.zh: 因此，这种奇怪的融合——这三位思想家深奥的主观理论，

sentences.en: violently compressed into the objective metrics of the military and the behaviorists that became what we know today, even though the language doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 被暴力压缩进军方和行为主义者的客观指标中，变成了我们今天所知的样子，尽管这些语言根本说不通。

sentences.en: And this is the moment that the world actually split.
sentences.zh: 这就是世界真正分裂的时刻。

sentences.en: The image of psychology began to divorce from the American reality of psychology.
sentences.zh: 心理学的形象开始与美国的心理学现实分道扬镳。

sentences.en: And talking about psychology from this point onward becomes a hall of mirrors.
sentences.zh: 从这一点开始谈论心理学，就变成了一座镜厅。

sentences.en: Just like the end of the first episode, we're left living inside of a ghost story here.
sentences.zh: 就像第一集结尾一样，我们在这里生活在一个鬼故事里。

sentences.en: The theories forged in 1920 and 1945, and the manufactured normalcy, the behavioral metrics, the lie that systemic poverty is a personal psychological defect, still haunt us today.
sentences.zh: 1920年和1945年锻造的理论，以及被制造出来的常态、行为指标、关于“系统性贫困是个人心理缺陷”的谎言，至今仍困扰着我们。

sentences.en: They still organize our lives, and their conclusions are baked into the very foundation of modern American psychology,
sentences.zh: 它们依然在组织我们的生活，它们的结论被植入现代美国心理学的根基之中，

sentences.en: even though our culture has long since canceled their premises, and modern science has found them scientifically useless.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们的文化早已否定了它们的前提，现代科学也发现它们在科学上毫无用处。

sentences.en: We're still being diagnosed by the ghost of World War II military logisticians.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然被二战军事后勤人员的幽灵所诊断。

sentences.en: Scientifically, the 1945 paradigm has been completely obliterated, yet the institutions that govern mental health, the American Psychiatric Association,
sentences.zh: 从科学上讲，1945年的范式已经被彻底摧毁，然而管理心理健康的机构——美国精神医学学会、

sentences.en: the managed care networks, the university training models, are locked into an infrastructure trap.
sentences.zh: 管理式医疗网络、大学培训模式——都被锁定在一个基础设施陷阱中。

sentences.en: They cannot abandon these mid-century metrics, because the entire economic architecture of American healthcare relies on them.
sentences.zh: 他们无法放弃这些中世纪的指标，因为美国医疗保健的整个经济架构都依赖于它们。

sentences.en: And the DSM is not just a clinical document.
sentences.zh: DSM不仅仅是一份临床文件。

sentences.en: It's a financial instrument.
sentences.zh: 它是一个金融工具。

sentences.en: And the bureaucracy demands a standardized measurable normal to process claims, allocate resources, and conduct pharmacological research.
sentences.zh: 官僚机构需要一个标准化的、可衡量的“正常”来处理索赔、分配资源和进行药理学研究。

sentences.en: The ghost of the 1940s isn't a statue or an ideal anymore.
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代的幽灵不再是一座雕像或一种理想。

sentences.en: It is a statistical mean against which all human suffering must be plotted and billed.
sentences.zh: 它是一个统计平均值，所有人类的痛苦都必须被绘制在这个平均值之上并据此计费。

sentences.en: And this requirement for measurable normalcy, combined with the logical efficiency of the military, created the ultimate pressure cooker.
sentences.zh: 这种对可衡量常态的要求，结合军方的逻辑效率，创造了一个终极的高压锅。

sentences.en: And as the troops came home, this exact combination laid the stage for white flight, and the birth of the American suburb.
sentences.zh: 随着军队回家，这种精确的组合为“白人群飞”和美国郊区的诞生奠定了基础。

sentences.en: Millions of Americans fled the cities, not just to find a patch of grass, but to frantically prove to the system, to their neighbors and to themselves, that they fit the metric.
sentences.zh: 数百万美国人逃离城市，不仅是为了寻找一片草地，更是为了疯狂地向体制、向邻居、向自己证明，他们符合那个指标。

sentences.en: In our next episode, we'll follow the ghosts into the 1950s, we'll enter the plastic oasis of the American suburb,
sentences.zh: 在下一集中，我们将跟随这些幽灵进入20世纪50年代，我们将进入美国郊区的塑料绿洲，

sentences.en: and we'll see what happens when the military's normal becomes mandatory, when the mind is reduced to a computer,
sentences.zh: 我们将看到当军方的“正常”成为强制要求，当心智被简化为计算机时会发生什么，

sentences.en: and when a generation desperately tries and fails to break out of the little boxes on the hillside.
sentences.zh: 以及当一代人绝望地试图逃离山坡上那些小盒子却最终失败时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Cold machines, warm ghosts, we're humming under power lines, your soft, sad, laughing, get carried through the tangled wires.
sentences.zh: 冰冷的机器，温暖的幽灵，我们在高压线下低吟，你那温柔、忧伤、欢笑的声音，正穿过错综复杂的电线传向远方。

sentences.en: Cold machines, warm ghosts, you singing something in me breaks, I'm holding on.
sentences.zh: 冰冷的机器，温暖的幽灵，你唱出的旋律让我内心某处破碎，我正努力支撑。

sentences.en: Hey guys, thank you for listening to part two of Psychotherapy on the Couch, a Psychohistory of American Psychology.
sentences.zh: 嘿，大家好，感谢收听《沙发上的心理治疗》第二部分，这是一部美国心理学的心灵史。

sentences.en: If you have not already, please check out our website, gettherapybirmingham.com, and consider subscribing to the podcast in your favorite podcast library or on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没听过，请访问我们的网站 gettherapybirmingham.com，并考虑在您常用的播客平台或 YouTube 上订阅我们的节目。
